Looking at the right hand side of the slide you can see that our corporate exposure is 79% investment grade. In 
the quarter, corporate nonaccrual loans as well as corporate net credit losses remained low. We are confident 
in the high-quality nature of our portfolios, which reflect our robust risk appetite framework and rigorous client 
selection. 
 
Turning to capital, liquidity and the balance sheet on Slide 7, speaking to sequential variances. Our total assets 
of $2.9 trillion increased 2%, driven by growth in trading -related assets and loans. Net end -of-period loans 
increased 3%, driven by growth in Markets and Banking. Our $1.5 trillion deposit base remains well diversified 
and increased 1%, primarily driven by growth in Services. We reported a 114% average LCR and over $1 trillion of 
available liquidity resources.

overall performance continues to demonstrate the disciplined and consistent execution of our strategy. 
 
Now let's go through our five businesses. This was another standout quarter in Services, with revenues up 15%.

In U.S. Consumer Cards, revenues were flat as a result of higher partner payments. At the same time, our

business, both through our deep relationships with key partners and differentiated rewards for our customers, 
as you saw with the acquisition of Kard. With returns of over 21% in the quarter, this is already a very attractive 
business, and the benefits of our investments will continue to scale overtime.
